As teens, and for some, even as a kid, we have often heard the ‘adults’ tell us, “You ain’t mature, child, grow up first.” But grow up, what does this actually refer to. Does it really mean to spend more time alive on this planet earth to increase our year count or does this grow up refers to something else? If else, then, will the adults really measure it up to know whether we are grown up or not regardless of our age?

I won’t deny the facts. With experience comes intellect, and with intellect comes the power to choose wisely and to know what and when to pursue whatever one wants to pursue. In short, ‘maturity’. But what is age’s relation with maturity? It is clear that both are different entities yet both have some sort of relation. Okay not some sort of relation but a very definitive one.

We often see grown-ups acting immature, and many teens and children pretty mature to their age. Why so? Every human has a different essence in this world, a different perspective and a vision on what to see, yet the society wants to enchain those sentiments and outlooks by set boring morals, which in this topic I mean, is the age and its relation with maturity. Age, your time spent alive has nothing to do with maturity. Teen’s often known as irrational, and often true as well, are labelled to be the most immature of the bunch due to their hyper. But, there exist this phenomenon, that your power, to have a control over yourself is maturity itself. The so called ‘adults’ won’t see it, but it’s there, it’s in one’s hand. Your maturity is how well you can define yourself and how true you stand with it, and age has nothing to do with it.

In short, I would conclude with my own quote, (yes I’m bragging); “Age is but the perspective of how you see this world, not the time you spend breathing alive.”
